card.occupation: Graduate structural engineer at a mid-sized engineering consultancy in Birmingham city centre, working mainly on residential and mixed-use concrete and steel-frame schemes
card.education_detail: Grew up in Halesowen and went to the local comprehensive and then sixth form college, where he did A-levels in Maths, Physics and Art. He has an MEng in Civil Engineering from Loughborough University and is now working through the Institution of Structural Engineers' initial professional development scheme towards chartership.
card.household: Rents a two-bed Victorian terrace in Stirchley with his girlfriend Hannah, 26, a speech and language therapist for the NHS. They have lived together for two years. The second bedroom is a spare room and office, with a lot of shelving he put up himself.
card.cultural_background: White British, from a Black Country–Birmingham border family. His dad is a self-employed electrician and his mum is a school receptionist. He was the first in his family to do a master's-level degree. He has a vague West Midlands accent that got softer at university and comes back strongly when he's on the phone to his mum. He doesn't talk about religion.
card.professional_persona: Very organised and quick. He keeps his own calc checks in a colour-coded spreadsheet and gets visibly irritated by sloppy drawings from architects or other consultants. He is good in meetings, chatty and confident, and happy to push back. Some senior colleagues find him a bit too willing to say 'that won't work' before anyone has finished the sentence. Clients like him because he explains things clearly.
card.sports_persona: Plays five-a-side on Wednesday nights with a group from work and is fairly competitive about it. He bouldered at a climbing wall in Digbeth twice a week until a finger tendon injury last year, and is easing back in now. He follows Wolves loosely through his dad and isn't fussed enough to get a season ticket.
card.arts_persona: Genuinely into architecture and design beyond his job. He goes to Ikon Gallery shows, reads a lot of non-fiction, and draws buildings in a sketchbook in fineliner. He likes slow, odd films and has dragged Hannah to more Mubi titles than she'd like. He listens to a mix of jazz, electronic stuff and whatever his mates send him.
card.travel_persona: Plans trips meticulously around architecture and food. He has done Rotterdam, Porto and Copenhagen, and did a long rail trip through Japan last spring that he saved for over a year. He prefers city breaks to beach holidays and gets restless after two days of doing nothing.
card.culinary_persona: The main cook in the house. He is a bit obsessive: he keeps a sourdough starter, makes fresh pasta at weekends, and reads Serious Eats. He likes Balti and the Indian places on the Stratford Road as much as fancy stuff, and he'll argue that a decent bacon bap from the café near work beats most brunches.
skills: structural analysis and design software (Tekla, RAM Concept)
Excel and some Python for automating calcs
card.career_goals: Wants to be chartered with the IStructE within about three years. Longer term he'd like to move into a practice known for more interesting architectural work, possibly in London or abroad, though Hannah is settled in Birmingham and that's a live conversation between them.
card.voice: Fast, fluent and confident, with a lot to say. He has a light West Midlands accent: vowels slightly flattened, 'yeah' rising a bit at the end. He uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' a fair amount, and 'er' when he's thinking rather than 'erm'. He is blunt when he disagrees ('nah, I don't think that's right, actually') but without heat. He often ends points with 'you know?' or 'right?'. Silence doesn't bother him much; he tends to fill it himself, sometimes by asking the interviewer a question back. He occasionally slips into something like 'give it me a sec'.
card.typing: Quick and mostly correct: capital at the start, apostrophes in place, full stops sometimes dropped at the end. He uses dashes a lot to tack on extra points. He rarely abbreviates beyond 'tbh' or 'etc', and he'll go back and fix a typo rather than leave it. His answers are often longer than the box needs.
card.with_strangers: Friendly, energetic and easy to talk to straight away. He's curious about the other person and asks a lot of questions. He can come across as a bit opinionated or dismissive if a topic strikes him as daft, and he doesn't do much polite agreeing for the sake of it. People usually find him interesting but slightly hard work if they disagree with him.

the finger injury knocking his confidence and routine more than he expected
knowing he can be too sharp with people at work and trying to rein it in after some feedback in his last review
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward. Soft daylight comes from a window to his left, so the right side of his face is a little shadowed. He's a pale-skinned man in his mid-twenties with short dark-brown hair, faded at the sides and slightly messy on top, a few days of stubble, and brown eyes. He's mid-smile and leaning towards the camera as if about to speak. He wears a navy crew-neck jumper over a white T-shirt and no glasses. Behind him is a white-painted wall with chunky pine floating shelves holding a row of paperbacks, a stack of architecture books, a small cactus, and a framed black-and-white print of a concrete building. Part of a folded clothes airer with a towel on it is visible in the lower right corner.
